//: Going without food (16 §9.5, decision D-906): what an empty `nourishment` pool does, written as traits and one rule; the engine knows nothing of hunger. The pool falls by about two parts in a hundred an hour, so a person who starts fed (70) is hungry below a quarter after about a day, weak below a tenth some seven hours later, and starving at nothing some five hours after that. Starving drains blood faster than the body makes it: about a day later the body falls (the blood pool's stop below 60%), and half a day after that it dies. Eating lifts the pool past a threshold and the trait for where it now stands replaces the last; above a quarter there is none. The three traits are one group, so a character has at most one. Values are illustrative.
name: Hungry
description: An empty stomach, and a little less in the arms.

name: Weak with hunger
description: Slow and feeble for want of food.

name: Starving
description: The body is eating itself: it will fall, and then die, unless it is fed.

doc: A character someone plays whose nourishment crossed a threshold takes the hunger trait for the band it is now in: falling below a quarter `hungry`, below a tenth `weak_with_hunger`, to nothing `starving`; rising off nothing `weak_with_hunger`, to a tenth `hungry`, to a quarter none. The town's residents are taken to eat at home, and are left out: their meals are not modelled.

do.if: (event.rising and event.threshold > 0.05 and event.threshold < 0.2) or (not event.rising and event.threshold > 0.2)
(event.rising and event.threshold < 0.05) or (not event.rising and event.threshold > 0.05 and event.threshold < 0.2)
